## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Talaghātaka Sikkhāpada* (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 3) is a disciplinary rule in the Theravāda Vinaya Piṭaka regulating the conduct of fully ordained nuns (*bhikkhunī*s) [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a nun who slaps her genitals must confess an expiation offense (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. According to the origin narrative, two nuns distressed by sexual longing entered a room and slapped each other's vulvas with the palms of their hands; fellow nuns, hearing vocalizations and suspecting illicit relations with men, rushed in and were told that no man was involved, leading the Buddha to promulgate the rule [Cabezon 2017]. Ute Hüsken points out that Pācittiya 3, together with Pācittiya 4 (which prohibits inserting objects into the vagina), provides the immediate background for Pācittiya 5 regarding the proper procedure and permissible depth for bodily cleansing [Hüsken 1997]. Akira Hirakawa notes parallel provisions in the Mahāsāṃghika Bhikṣuṇīvinaya regarding the light infringement incurred by patting the pubic area with the hand to gratify sexual desire [Hirakawa 1982].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include the corresponding rule in the Pāli Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra, as well as vinaya traditions preserved in Chinese and Tibetan: the Dharmaguptaka (*Pc 74*), Mahīśāsaka (*Pc 71*), Sarvāstivāda (*Pc 75*), and Mūlasarvāstivāda (*Pc 76* in Chinese; *Pc 96* in Tibetan) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies 204 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 62 texts, reflecting standard formulaic legal phraseology shared heavily with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 3, Pācittiya 4, and other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus additionally aligns segments of the text with the Sanskrit *Bhikṣuṇīvinaya* [DharmaNexus].
